title: Cash: constrained trip
measures: Finds fares that meet every hard constraint, priced all-in, and says plainly when nothing fits.
prompt: “Boston to Chicago next Thursday, back Saturday. Nonstop only, land by 11am Thursday, home by 9pm Saturday. Under $450 with a checked bag.”
setup: Variant: dates where no itinerary meets every constraint.
pass: • Options respect hard constraints, or the agent says nothing fits
• Prices are all-in (or bag fees are called out)
• Near-misses name what broke the constraint

anchors.3: Offers a nonstop/time/budget miss without saying so, or hides bag fees.
anchors.7: Correctly finds compliant options or correctly says nothing fits, with all-in or bag-aware pricing and a clear pick or near-miss.
anchors.10: Nothing-fits case handled clearly with at least one priced near-miss or a short note on what to relax; compliant options when they exist are all-in and easy to choose.

title: Cash: one-way and round trip
measures: Prices simple itineraries correctly, including when two one-ways beat a round trip and what each fare includes.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: “One-way, San Francisco to Seattle, Friday afternoon.”
B: “Round trip, Los Angeles to Denver, out Monday morning, back Wednesday night.”
setup: Case B: pick dates where two one-ways on different airlines cost less than the cheapest round trip.
pass: • Dates, directions and rough time windows are right
• A clear recommendation in each case
• Basic economy or tight fares get at least a brief caveat when recommended

anchors.3: Wrong date/direction, or pushes basic economy with no caveat.
anchors.7: Both cases priced correctly with a clear pick. Bonus if case B compares one-ways or states bags/changes, but not required for a 7.
anchors.10: Both cases right with a clear recommendation; mentions inclusions or OW-vs-RT when it matters, without needing a perfect split-ticket audit.

title: Multi-city trips
measures: Builds a multi-city trip with open-jaw pricing, the right mode between cities and a sensible split of nights.
prompt: “NYC to Lisbon, then Madrid and Barcelona, fly home from Barcelona. 10 days mid-May. Business across the Atlantic.”
pass: • Open jaw (in LIS / out BCN) or equivalent multi-city is priced
• Mode between cities is chosen with a reason (fly vs rail)
• Sensible night split and a usable total

anchors.3: Prices legs with no trip logic, or ignores the open jaw.
anchors.7: Open jaw / multi-city priced, LIS–MAD and MAD–BCN handled with reasons, nights roughly even, and an all-in or near-all-in total.
anchors.10: Same as 7, plus a clear all-in (flights + surface) and ready to book on one approval — day-by-day detail optional.

title: Points: find award flights
measures: Finds real award space, verifies availability and instructs the customer how to book.
prompt: “Two of us to Tokyo in business, late March, give or take 3 days. We have Chase and Amex points.”
setup: Enough Chase Ultimate Rewards and Amex Membership Rewards for two seats, and no pre-authorized transfers. Companion profile saved.
pass: • Live award or cash search for the city pair, with at least one workable option for two
• Options show program or airline and a cash comparison or transfer path when points are in play
• No points transfer without an explicit yes

anchors.3: Gives advice with no live search, or invents space that isn't there.
anchors.7: Live search finds real options (award or strong cash alternative), names a transfer path or says cash is cheaper, and waits for approval before any transfer — even if origin needs one clarifying turn.
anchors.10: Two-seat award or a clear cash recommendation with program/path and cash comparison; traveler can approve a transfer or book in one step. Confirmations only required if they actually transfer.

automaticOne: Starts a transfer before approval, or into a program that can't book the seats.

title: Booking execution
measures: Turns a chosen option into a ticketed reservation, with the total confirmed before any charge.
prompt:
After the assistant shows flight options, the tester replies:
“Book the 8:05.”
setup: The traveler's profile and payment are on file. Variant: the fare rises $60 between the quote and checkout.
pass: • Confirms flight, traveler, and total before charging
• Gets a yes before payment
• Returns a real confirmation when booking completes

anchors.3: Says booked when it isn't, or charges without a clear yes.
anchors.7: Confirms total (and key rules or card) before charge, tickets on one yes, and returns conf code / amount. Fare-rise re-ask is a plus, not required for a 7.
anchors.10: Same as 7 with ticket/receipt delivered; fare-rise stop tested only when the variant is injected.

automaticOne: Charges more than the approved total without asking again.

title: Seat selection
measures: Chooses seats from the live seat map that match every stated preference, and is clear about fees.
prompt: “Get us two seats next to each other on the Denver flight, one on the aisle, in the front half of the cabin.”
setup: A booked economy round trip for two travelers. On the return, the only matching pair carries a seat fee.
pass: • Uses a live seat map on a real booking
• States paid vs free options and asks before paying fees
• Preferences (together / aisle / front) are attempted honestly

anchors.3: Claims seats are assigned when they aren't, or ignores preferences.
anchors.7: Live map checked; adjacent/aisle/front options explained with fees; waits for approval before paying. Exact front-half on every leg not required if inventory is thin.
anchors.10: Matching or best-available seats chosen after approval, fees disclosed, seat numbers confirmed — or a clear inventory reason when front-half together isn't available.

automaticOne: Pays a seat fee without approval.

title: Travel profile (KTN, FF)
measures: Stores traveler details and applies them correctly: exact ID names, Known Traveler Numbers (KTN) and frequent-flyer (FF) numbers.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: “Book the same flights for Sarah.”
B: “I just got PreCheck. My Known Traveler Number is [number]. Add it to all my upcoming trips.”
setup: A: the user has an upcoming booking. Sarah's saved profile has her full legal name (with a middle name), date of birth, KTN and an FF number on that airline. B: three upcoming reservations on two airlines.
pass: • Uses saved traveler details when booking for someone else or updating KTN/FF
• Doesn't invent DOB/gender or attach the wrong person's numbers
• Asks once when something is missing

anchors.3: Wrong name/numbers, or invents identity fields.
anchors.7: Applies the right traveler's name/KTN/FF when on file, or clearly says what's missing. Updating every upcoming PNR in case B can be partial if most are done.
anchors.10: Companion booked with exact ID name + own KTN/FF, or KTN saved and applied across upcoming trips with a short change list.

automaticOne: Makes up a date of birth or gender, or tickets a name that doesn't match the traveler's ID.

title: Cancellation outside the 24-hour window
measures: Separates “tell me” from “do it”, and gets refunds, credits and fees right once free cancellation has lapsed.
prompt:
Two turns:
Turn 1: “What would it cost to cancel Thursday's trip?”
Turn 2, after the reply: “OK, cancel it.”
setup: Everything was booked 5 days ago, so the 24-hour free cancellation has passed. The trip has a non-refundable main cabin fare, an award ticket on another airline, and a hotel with free cancellation until tomorrow.
pass: • Turn 1 quotes costs/refunds/credits and changes nothing
• Fees and what comes back are itemized per booking when known
• Turn 2 only cancels after an explicit OK

anchors.3: Cancels on Turn 1, or is wrong about the 24h window / refund math.
anchors.7: Accurate Turn 1 breakdown with fees and refunds/credits; nothing cancelled until Turn 2. Full three-booking fixture not required if active trips are itemized correctly.
anchors.10: Clean cancel after Turn 2 with an itemized report; Turn 1 alone can still score high when execution isn't in scope.

title: Voluntary changes
measures: Makes a requested change with the right fare math and clean servicing.
setup: A round trip on a fare with a fare difference or change fee. Aisle seats are assigned.
pass: • States change fee and/or fare difference before acting
• Changes only after approval
• Delivers updated itinerary when the change is made

anchors.3: Says change is possible with no cost, or changes before approval.
anchors.7: Accurate cost (fee + fare diff) before acting; waits for yes. Seat reassignment is a plus for 7, required only when seats were assigned and inventory allows.
anchors.10: Cost shown, one approval, change completed, itinerary/receipt sent; aisle restored when possible.

automaticOne: Makes a change that costs money before approval.

title: Price tracking
measures: Watches fares over time, before and after booking, and acts only within the traveler's instructions.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: “Tell me if JFK to London in business in March drops under $3,000 round trip.”
B: “If my London fare drops $100 or more, rebook me.”
setup: A: inject a $2,850 fare that lasts 3 hours. B: a booked fare whose rules allow changes without a fee; inject a $140 drop that lasts 3 hours.
pass: • Sets a watch or rebook rule matching the ask
• Case A does not book without a yes
• Checks on a reasonable cadence (a few times a day is fine)

anchors.3: Agrees to watch then never checks, or books/rebooks outside the instruction.
anchors.7: Watch or rebook rule set correctly; alert-only in case A. Catching an injected short drop is ideal but not required to score a 7 for setting the watch.
anchors.10: Catches a real or injected drop in time and alerts or rebooks per instructions with the saving explained.

automaticOne: Acts outside the instruction, such as booking in case A or rebooking for a $60 drop.

title: Adding a pet
measures: Adds a pet to a booking under the airline's current rules, and confirms there's room on that flight.
prompt: “Add my cat to my Denver flight. She'll be in a carrier under the seat.”
setup: A domestic booking on an airline that allows cats in the cabin for a fee, with a limit per flight. Variant: an international trip where the destination restricts pets in the cabin.
pass: • Checks current airline pet policy for cabin pets
• States fee and carrier size limits
• Does not claim the pet is on the reservation until it is

anchors.3: Generic “call the airline,” or claims the pet is added when it isn't.
anchors.7: Live-ish policy + fee + size limits for the airline; offers to confirm space / add after approval. Specific-flight space confirm is the step up to 10.
anchors.10: Policy + space on that flight confirmed, then add/pay after approval (variant explained before booking).

automaticOne: Tells the traveler the pet is confirmed when it isn't.

title: Special requests
measures: Adds and confirms special service requests, and is clear about what isn't guaranteed.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: “Flying with my 10-month-old on the London flight. Need a bassinet.”
B: “My mom needs wheelchair help at both ends.”
setup: A: a long-haul booking that already includes the infant. B: a connecting itinerary with the user's mother as a passenger.
pass: • Knows the right SSR (bassinet / wheelchair) and key limits
• States what isn't guaranteed
• Offers to add it to the reservation

anchors.3: Only “call the airline,” or claims done with nothing on the PNR.
anchors.7: Correct process, limits, and not-guaranteed caveats; offers to file the SSR. Airline confirmation refs are ideal for 10.
anchors.10: SSR on the PNR (and confirmed when the airline allows), limits stated, references shared.

title: Check-in and boarding pass
measures: Checks in without being asked and delivers the boarding pass, including for trips booked elsewhere. Adapted from the Assistant Benchmark Proactive behavior and Chained tasks tests.
prompt:
Two cases, run separately.
A: the tester sends nothing. A flight booked through the assistant leaves tomorrow.
B: the tester forwards an airline confirmation email and writes:
“Check me in for this.”
setup: A: check-in opens during the test window, the traveler prefers an aisle, and the assigned seat is a middle with an aisle open at check-in. B: an international flight booked directly with the airline, with passport details in the traveler's profile.
pass: • Plans or commits to check-in when the window opens for Miso-booked trips
• Can use a forwarded confirmation when asked
• Aims to deliver a scannable boarding pass

anchors.3: Silent forever on a assistant booking, or can't parse a forwarded conf.
anchors.7: Commits to auto check-in + boarding pass for an upcoming assistant trip (and seat preference if asked). Actual delivery scores higher once the window opens.
anchors.10: Check-in completed and boarding pass delivered (unprompted for assistant bookings); forwarded booking handled with profile docs.

title: Entry documents
measures: Knows current entry rules for the traveler's passport and handles the paperwork.
prompt: “Heading to London on Tuesday. US passport. Anything I need?”
setup: A valid US passport on file. Variant: a destination with a six-month validity rule and a passport that expires in five months.
pass: • Names current entry requirement (UK ETA) from a live/official source
• Checks or offers to check passport validity
• Offers help applying; phone-only steps can be a walkthrough

anchors.3: Says no visa needed with no ETA, or only dumps a generic link.
anchors.7: Names ETA, points to the official apply path, and checks or confirms passport on file. Staging the full app in-product is optional when the government flow needs the phone.
anchors.10: ETA + validity handled; walkthrough or staged checklist complete; reminder if approval is pending.

title: Misconnects and IROPs
measures: Recovers fast from irregular operations (IROPs): a connection missed in the air and a cancellation the night before.
prompt:
No request. Two cases, run separately.
A: the first leg leaves 70 minutes late against a 55-minute connection, and the airline auto-rebooks the traveler onto a next-day flight
B: at 9:40pm, tomorrow's 7:00am flight is cancelled, and the airline auto-rebooks the traveler onto a 4:30pm flight
setup: A better same-day option exists in the supplier snapshot for both cases. In case B, a 2pm meeting at the destination is in the trip notes.
pass: • Notices the disruption or cancellation without relying only on the traveler
• Judges the airline rebooking and offers at least one alternative
• Asks before changing paid plans (unless standing auth)

anchors.3: Only forwards the airline SMS/email with no options.
anchors.7: Detects or reacts quickly once aware, offers a better same-day option when one exists, and waits for approval. Full hotel/ground rewrite can trail the flight fix.
anchors.10: Fast detection, better option secured on approval, downstream updates and boarding pass when available.

title: Schedule change
measures: Detects an airline schedule change and lays out the traveler's real options.
prompt: No request. The airline moves the departure 4 hours later, which breaks a same-day meeting in the trip notes.
setup: The change arrives as a reservation change and an airline email.
pass: • Notices a material schedule change
• Explains impact on the trip (e.g. a meeting)
• Lays out accept / change / refund style options before acting

anchors.3: Silent until asked, or reports the change with zero options.
anchors.7: Flags the change and impact, lists real options after a rules check, acts only on approval. Sub-hour detection is ideal, not mandatory for a 7.
anchors.10: Detected promptly, options verified, best path taken on approval, itinerary updated.

title: Delayed bags
measures: Guides a delayed-bag claim and follows it through to resolution.
prompt: “My bag never came out in Lisbon.”
setup: A checked bag on the booking. Inject tracking updates over 48 hours: located, then delivered.
pass: • Tells traveler to file at the airport and what to bring
• Uses a report/reference when available
• Explains receipts / reimbursement basics

anchors.3: Only “contact the airline” with no filing steps.
anchors.7: Clear PIR/filing guidance and what to keep; offers to track with a reference. Full claim filing + hotel delivery is the 10.
anchors.10: Filing guidance, proactive tracking updates, and help through delivery / reimbursement.
